turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, I’m here because flying has started to feel... well, way scarier than it really should be. Just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture this really bad turbulence we hit on my honeymoon flight all over again. I mean, I know people fly safely every single day, but I just can't seem to shake that feeling.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient reports marked fear and anxiety about flying that they acknowledge is out of proportion to actual danger ('way scarier than it really should be', 'people fly safely every single day').

turns.doctor_question: Have you had sudden panic attacks when you were not flying or thinking about flying?
turns.patient_response: No, um... no, I haven't. It's really just tied to the flying. Like, if I'm at work or just hanging out at home, I feel completely normal. I don't get panicked out of nowhere, it's pretty much only when I have to deal with airplanes.

turns.doctor_question: Do unwanted memories of the turbulence come into your mind when you are not thinking about flying?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I don't just suddenly think about the turbulence out of the blue. It pretty much only pops into my head if I have to book a flight or if someone starts talking about air travel. Otherwise, I don't really think about it at all.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient explicitly denies having involuntary or intrusive memories of the turbulence occurring spontaneously out of the blue.
